mode: reference-guided generation with targeted projection edits
request: Generate a 2D top, bottom, side, back, and front reference of the Cruiser.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: 2D orthographic spaceship reference sheet for modeling the existing Stellar Syndicates CRUISER.

Primary request: Create ONE polished reference image with exactly FIVE complete, consistent views of the SAME cruiser: TOP, BOTTOM, SIDE, BACK, and FRONT. This will guide a fully textured 3D reconstruction, so the underside must be as carefully finished as the top.

Input images:
Image 1 is the authoritative top-down CRUISER design. Preserve its outline, proportions, armor layout and equipment positions.
Image 2 is supporting three-quarter CRUISER reference for depth, thickness and materials only. Do not copy its perspective.
Image 3 is the existing INTERCEPTOR reference sheet, a STYLE AND PRESENTATION reference only. Do not borrow the interceptor's geometry.

Cruiser identity: long sharp central wedge prow; broad swept armored shoulders widening toward mid-aft hull; raised compact faceted command bridge on the centerline; exactly TWO dorsal turrets, one per shoulder, each with TWO forward-pointing barrels; two deep recessed aft side bays; central longitudinal armored service spine; exactly FOUR cylindrical stern engines in a horizontal row, the inner pair larger than the outer pair; narrow tapered center tail between the inner engines. Preserve original bay detail and the dark spaces separating the machinery. No enlarged cockpit canopy or fighter-like delta wings. This is the existing heavy cruiser, not a redesign.

Composition: generous wide LANDSCAPE canvas, approximately 2:1 aspect, high native resolution and crisp detail. Clean warm-white background. Two tall plan drawings fill the left and middle: TOP on the left, BOTTOM beside it, both noses pointing straight UP and both the same length and width. A generous right-hand column contains FRONT at the top, BACK in the middle, and SIDE at the bottom. SIDE points LEFT and spans the width of its column. Use enough canvas space that the side's nose-to-tail length equals the top and bottom lengths; front and back widths equal the plan-view beam. Keep all drawings complete, with generous margins and clear separation. A restrained title at upper left, simple labels beneath each view. Exactly five drawings and six text labels.

Style: match the interceptor sheet's precise 2D colored hard-surface drafting. Thin crisp charcoal contours, pale titanium and silver-gray armor plates, charcoal gunmetal structure, restrained warm brass fittings, fine cyan luminous strips, clear panel seams, only gentle neutral shading to explain form. Mild surface wear matching the cruiser reference; no dramatic studio lighting or photorealistic beauty render.

Projection rules are critical:
TOP: true straight overhead, zero yaw or pitch. Bilateral symmetry. Keep the exact pointed cruiser planform and both two-barrel dorsal turrets. Cylindrical engines appear as longitudinal housings terminating in narrow rear rims; do not rotate their round exhaust faces upward toward this camera.
BOTTOM: true straight underneath, zero perspective, nose UP. Identical outer silhouette and four engine locations as TOP. Show genuinely distinct ventral construction: silver-gray belly armor, dark recessed central keel, articulated panel seams, flush maintenance hatches, segmented thermal/radiator panels, restrained brass locks and small cyan service lights. Continue all surface textures to the edges. No empty or featureless gray underside. Do not stamp the bridge, upper gun turrets, cockpit glazing, or open dorsal bays onto the belly. Do not add landing legs, extra weapons, or unrelated protrusions.
FRONT: exact level head-on orthographic elevation, camera on the nose axis at ZERO elevation. The long fore-aft dimension collapses completely. A shallow broad armored hull, small central nose tip and raised bridge behind it, low sloping shoulders, the two dorsal turret assemblies seen head-on with four small barrel ends. Fore/aft forms occlude each other naturally. No long nose blade viewed from above; no rear exhaust circles or cyan engine discs visible through the hull. No broad overhead view squeezed vertically.
BACK: exact level stern-on orthographic elevation, ZERO elevation, matching FRONT width and height. Exactly FOUR round cyan exhaust apertures with dark layered nozzle rims: two large inner apertures, two smaller outer apertures. Central keel tip between them; bridge and turrets rise above the stern silhouette. No perspective or top-down tail planform.
SIDE: strict level port-side orthographic profile with nose LEFT and stern RIGHT, ZERO yaw and ZERO elevation. A long low pointed wedge bow, sloping armor, modest raised bridge, near dorsal twin-barrel turret shown in overlapping profile, recessed near-side service bay, deep armored belly, engine housings running horizontally to vertical nozzle rims at the right. Symmetric far-side features overlap correctly. No visible broad roof, no front-facing circular exhaust discs, no isometric angle, no invented tall tail.

Consistency: All five drawings must describe one physically coherent ship. Match length, beam, height, bridge position, turret stations, shoulder geometry, bay stations, hull thickness and all four engine sizes/positions. Top and bottom panel treatment can differ, but silhouettes and structure must match. Infer hidden hull surfaces conservatively from the supplied cruiser.

Text (verbatim): "CRUISER", "TOP", "BOTTOM", "SIDE", "BACK", "FRONT".
Avoid: any sixth view, perspective inset, other free-standing ships, dimensions, scale numbers, invented specifications, cutaway, exploded parts, grid, scenery, starfield, floor, cast shadows, exhaust plumes, watermark, logos.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the five-view CRUISER reference sheet. Image 2 is the original cruiser identity reference.
Correct ONLY the projection and equipment orientation errors. Preserve the exact ship identity, materials, new detailed belly armor, title, all five labels, white background, clean technical-illustration style, and five-view layout. Keep TOP and BOTTOM armor designs and silhouettes.

The upper-right FRONT is currently an elevated overhead view compressed vertically. Replace it with a TRUE LEVEL HEAD-ON orthographic elevation at ZERO elevation and ZERO yaw. The longitudinal axis points straight out of the page and has NO visible length. The prow appears as a small blunt faceted nose end in the center, not a long vertical silver blade. Its tip overlaps the lower bridge; the compact bridge rises above the hull behind it. Wide swept shoulders are seen EDGE-ON as thick low armor ledges, with two turret blocks above them and four tiny forward-facing gun muzzle ends. Eliminate the two forward-facing open hangar mouths and tiny ships: those are dorsal aft recesses and are occluded from the front. Eliminate the long downward central tail spike, dorsal top surfaces, and compressed roof planform. Show plausible broad gunmetal belly armor under the shallow shoulder contours. No exhaust apertures in FRONT.

In the middle-right BACK, KEEP exactly four cyan exhaust circles: two larger INNER engines and two smaller OUTER engines. Make this a true level stern-on orthographic elevation, rather than an elevated view. Critical correction: we are seeing the BACKS of the turret housings. Remove all four front-facing gun muzzle circles from this BACK view. Show solid squared rear turret housings, with the forward barrel length occluded behind them. Keep the engine order, centered keel between the inner engines, hull span and raised bridge. Do not add engines or turrets.

The lower-right SIDE has guns pointing the wrong way and exposes broad roof surfaces. Redraw it as an EXACT LEVEL LEFT SIDE profile, zero elevation, zero yaw, NO perspective. Nose LEFT, stern RIGHT. The two dorsal turrets occupy the SAME longitudinal station and therefore overlap in profile; show ONE near turret silhouette with its twin barrels overlapping in profile and pointing LEFT TOWARD THE NOSE, never toward the engines. Do not add a separate smaller side-mounted gun below the bridge. Far-side hull features overlap their near-side counterparts. Broad horizontal upper armor decks and open dorsal hangar floors cannot be seen from this zero-elevation camera. Show upper and lower contours, layered side plating, narrow side seams, recessed side machinery, low pointed prow, compact bridge, armored belly, and cylindrical engines from the side terminating in VERTICAL nozzle rims at the right. All four engines are side-by-side, not vertically stacked: in SIDE the smaller near engine and the larger inner engine overlap about one shared horizontal thrust centerline. No pair of engines stacked vertically; no front-facing circular exhaust discs. No tall fin.

In TOP and BOTTOM only flatten the rear engine projection if necessary: directly overhead/below, each cylinder is a longitudinal housing ending in an edge-on narrow rim. Do not show elliptical bright exhaust discs rotated toward these cameras. Preserve all other details of those two drawings, especially the fully designed BOTTOM.

Keep consistent scale: FRONT and BACK width should match the beam of the TOP drawing, and the SIDE nose-to-tail length should match the TOP length. FRONT and BACK heights match the SIDE hull/bridge height. Center the smaller corrected front/back drawings within their right column. Leave ample clear space between views and labels.
Text remains exactly "CRUISER", "TOP", "BOTTOM", "FRONT", "BACK", "SIDE". Exactly five consistent orthographic ship drawings. No added annotations or panels.

prompts.step: Correct side profile stations and front armor
prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit the supplied CRUISER five-view reference sheet. Make a final targeted correction to the lower-right SIDE drawing and two small areas of FRONT. Preserve the other drawings, all six labels, all material colors, the detailed BOTTOM, and the white page.

REPLACE THE SIDE DRAWING with a clean, geometrically correct left-side elevation. Do not retain the current side drawing's incorrect bridge and turret locations.
The bow is at the LEFT; the stern is at the RIGHT. Think of the length from nose to exhaust as a ruler from 0% to 100%:
- The low pointed armored prow occupies 0–20%.
- The command bridge stands at approximately 25–35% of ship length, well FORWARD of the turret.
- The one visible near-side turret is at approximately 45–55% of ship length, BEHIND the bridge. Its paired barrels run horizontally LEFT toward the nose. In strict side view the far turret is hidden behind this near turret. Never put the turret in front of the bridge.
- The broad shoulder and recessed flank machinery occupy 40–80%.
- The cylindrical engine and its side-profile nozzle occupy 80–100%.
- A low armored ventral keel runs below the body.
The side drawing must be a perfectly FLAT PROFILE: all long hull lines horizontal, camera at zero elevation and zero yaw. Show a single visible side surface, not the roof. Do not show broad trapezoidal top armor plates, a bird's-eye hangar floor, a second far-side shoulder, or top faces of engine cylinders.
There are four engines across the ship's width, sharing a horizontal thrust axis height. They OVERLAP in the side projection: show ONE main horizontal cylindrical engine silhouette at the stern with a vertical nozzle lip at the extreme right, plus at most a subtly inset smaller concentric profile. NO two vertically stacked engine tubes, no vertical exhaust array, no circular exhaust faces toward the viewer.
Remove the extra small side-mounted cannon/cyan barrel under the bridge. The original has only the two shoulder turrets. Use restrained armor panel lines and cooling vents in that area.
Retain the ship's very low, long wedge silhouette. Bridge should be the highest point, with turret slightly lower. No new fins or landing gear.

FRONT (upper-right): close the two black hangar-mouth openings and remove the tiny ships visible inside them. Replace ONLY those openings with matching closed, faceted gunmetal-and-titanium frontal armor panels. No open hangar mouths face the nose. Retain the small central nose tip, command bridge, four tiny gun muzzles, symmetrical shoulders and existing view label.

TOP, BOTTOM and BACK: preserve them unchanged. This remains one ship in exactly five views. Do not add a sixth drawing or any text.
